profile.name: Rainbow Children's Medicare Ltd
profile.founded: 1999, Banjara Hills, Hyderabad, by Dr Ramesh Kancharla (paediatric gastroenterologist trained in the UK)
profile.listing: IPO 27-29 Apr 2022 at ₹542 (₹1,581 cr: fresh issue ₹280 cr, offer for sale ~₹1,301 cr); listed 10-May-2022 at ₹510
profile.brands: Rainbow Children's Hospital (paediatrics); BirthRight by Rainbow (obstetrics, fetal medicine, fertility)
profile.network: 24 hospitals and 5 clinics in 9 cities (Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Guwahati, Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry, Warangal); 2,565 capacity beds incl. 130 beds at Madhukar, Malviya Nagar (Delhi) where Rainbow provides medical services; KPI beds exclude Madhukar: 2,435 capacity, 1,862 operational (Q1FY27)
profile.doctors: 1,075+ full-time doctors incl. residents and DNB trainees (Q1FY27); full-time, retainer-based, 24/7 consultant-led model; largest private paediatric DNB programme
profile.criticalCare: ~1/3 of beds allocated to critical care (NICU/PICU); level-4 NICU
profile.accreditation: 3 hospitals JCI (Banjara Hills, Marathahalli, BirthRight Fertility Kondapur); 14 NABH
profile.model: Hub and spoke: city hubs of 150-250 beds with tertiary/quaternary paediatric care (transplants, cardiac surgery, oncology, ECMO); spokes of 50-100 beds for emergency, OP, obstetrics and level-3 NICU; regional 'South Connect' spokes 200-250 km from hubs

annualKpiNote: opBedsAvg = weighted-average operational beds the company uses for occupancy (year-end operational beds: 1,523 at Mar-25, 1,806 at Mar-26). Occupancy = occupied bed days ÷ (weighted operational beds × days); ARPOB = total operating revenue ÷ occupied bed days (so it includes OP and pharmacy revenue); ALOS = occupied bed days ÷ IP discharges. Revenue = occupancy × beds × 365 × ARPOB reconciles to reported revenue within 0.3% in FY23-FY26.

quarterlyKpiSrc: Company earnings presentations Q2FY26 (Nov-2025), Q3FY26 (Jan-2026), Q4FY26 (23-May-2026), Q1FY27 (30-Jul-2026); prior-year columns for FY25 quarters. Values read from chart labels and checked against revenue (OBD × ARPOB).
seasonality: Paediatric demand peaks with monsoon and winter infections: Q2 and Q3 are the strong quarters (FY25: occupancy 59.9% in Q2 vs 46.5% in Q4). FY26 had a weak season: management says growth would have been 18-20% instead of 12% with normal seasonal demand (Q4FY26 call). Seasonal business historically ~10-12% of revenue (IIFL question, Q4FY26 call).

otherIncomeFy26.standaloneYieldOnInvestedFunds: Income from invested funds ₹365 cr ÷ average invested funds ₹7,175 mn = 5.1% in FY26 (7.4% in FY25), standalone ratio note
otherIncomeFy26.note: MD&A: other income fell because funds were used for the two acquisitions and projects. Treasury income (deposits + mutual funds) ₹38.4 cr in FY26 vs ₹46.9 cr in FY25; the rest (₹5.4 cr) is interest on loans/other financial assets, write-backs, an asset-sale gain and FX.

guidance.said: 'Aspirational yet achievable growth of 20% in the current year while maintaining margins' (CEO); FY26 would have grown 18-20% instead of 12% with a normal season (CMD)
Group occupancy of 56-58% is the level at which the model delivers its budgets (CMD)
ARPP (revenue per patient) to grow ~5-6% a year; ARPOB driven by case mix, fertility and price; fertility to grow ~25% a year for three years
guidance.outcome: Q1FY27 ARPOB +6%; mature units +10% (price and mix)

guidance.said: Maintenance ~₹45 cr a year; Gurugram ₹400-500 cr over two years (own land, own build); other projects ₹65-70 lakh a bed (~₹300-350 cr for ~450 beds); all from internal accruals
'We expect growth to remain above 20%' in Q2 (CEO)
FY27 revenue to cross ₹2,000 cr; potential to double in the following four years (~20% a year)
Pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin to return to 24-25% by the end of the year (CMD)
Add ~2,500 beds to reach ~5,000 in five years for ~₹2,200 cr of capex; 1,200 beds already visible; ~30% in existing southern markets, ~70% in new markets (NCR, North, Central India, Mumbai)

New Bengaluru units to break even in 12-15 months (all within ~18); Electronic City in 2-3 months; Rajahmundry at breakeven; Guwahati at company-average margins; Warangal to reach company margins over the next year
Malad (100 beds, JV with three doctor-promoters) to open in Q1FY28; EBITDA margin eventually above 20%
